title: Artin tensor acyclicity for strict-local algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $B_1,B_2$ be ind-etale $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Assume that each $\operatorname{Spec}(B_j)$ is etale acyclic, meaning every etale covering of it splits (equivalently, every connected component is strictly henselian). Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}(B_1\otimes_R B_2)$. Then for every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], one has $H^q(T_{\mathrm{Et}},F)=0$ for every $q>0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Hübner–Schmidt, Definition 7.8, Proposition 7.9 (étale case, after Artin, On the joins of Hensel rings, Proposition 3.2) and Theorem 7.10 (étale case), printed pp. 14–15. The passage from étale acyclicity to vanishing cohomology: since every étale covering of the affine scheme $T$ splits, $\Gamma(T,-)$ is exact on abelian sheaves, so its higher derived functors vanish, as in the last sentence of the proof of Stacks Project etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03QO.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-affine-etale-cover-component-criterion], the split-cover assumption makes every component ring of each $B_j$ strictly henselian, hence henselian local by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Also every maximal residue field $B_j/\mathfrak n$ is separably closed: the point $\mathfrak n$ belongs to a component $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B_j/I_Z)$, so $I_Z\subseteq\mathfrak n$. The quotient $\mathfrak n/I_Z$ is maximal in this local component ring and is therefore its unique maximal ideal. Its residue field $(B_j/I_Z)/(\mathfrak n/I_Z)=B_j/\mathfrak n$ is separably closed by strict henselianity. This uses no decomposition of $B_j$ as a product of its component rings.

source.place: Proposition 7.9 (etale case); component convention in §6, printed pp. 12 and 15

proof.text: Put $B=B_1\otimes_R B_2$. The hypotheses for [lem-trf-artin-henselian-tensor-residue-dichotomy] hold: the factors are ind-etale over the same ring $R$ as in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], and Step 1 supplies henselian local component rings. Thus every component ring of $B$ is henselian local. For each maximal $\mathfrak m\subset B$, the same node gives either a separably closed field $B/\mathfrak m$, or a separable algebraic extension $B_j/\mathfrak n\to B/\mathfrak m$ with $\mathfrak n$ maximal in one factor.

source.place: Theorem 6.4, printed p. 13, applied as in the first sentence of the proof of Theorem 7.10

proof.text: In the second case, $k=B_j/\mathfrak n$ is separably closed by Step 1. Every element $a$ of the separable algebraic extension $L=B/\mathfrak m$ has irreducible separable minimal polynomial over $k$; such a polynomial is linear over a separably closed field, so $a\in k$ and $k\to L$ is an isomorphism. Thus all maximal residue fields of $B$ are separably closed in both cases. If $D=B/I_Z$ is any component ring, its unique maximal ideal pulls back to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$, and $D/\mathfrak m_D=B/\mathfrak m$. Step 2 and [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] now make $D$ strictly henselian. Apply [lem-trf-affine-etale-cover-component-criterion] to $B$: every etale covering family of $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$ has a section after disjoint union.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 7.10, residue-field cases (1) and (2), and Proposition 7.9, printed p. 15

proof.text: Let $\varphi:G\to H$ be any epimorphism of abelian sheaves on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, and let $h\in H(T)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], there is an etale covering family $\{U_a\to T\}$ with lifts $g_a\in G(U_a)$ of $h|_{U_a}$. Choose its section $s:T\to\coprod_a U_a$ from Step 3 and set $T_a=s^{-1}(U_a)$. These are pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subsets covering $T$, with maps $s_a:T_a\to U_a$ over $T$. The sections $s_a^*g_a$ glue to $g\in G(T)$ by the sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]; on empty intersections all restrictions agree. Naturality gives $\varphi(g)|_{T_a}=h|_{T_a}$, hence $\varphi(g)=h$ by the same sheaf condition. Evaluation at the terminal object is $\Gamma(T,-)$ [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor], so it preserves epimorphisms. It preserves kernels because these are computed sectionwise [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel], and it is additive since morphisms and restrictions are group homomorphisms. It is therefore exact on abelian sheaves.

source.place: Tags 03CN (lemma-abelian-abelian), (5), and 03CO (lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves), (2); split-cover argument generalizing etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03QO

proof.text: For the given torsion abelian sheaf $F$, choose the resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ used in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. It is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], so $\mathcal H^q(I^\bullet)=0$ for $q>0$, since $F$ starts in degree zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to the exact additive functor $\Gamma(T,-)$ from Step 4. For $q>0$ this gives $H^q(T_{\mathrm{Et}},F)=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,I^\bullet))\cong\Gamma(T,\mathcal H^q(I^\bullet))=0$. Torsion was not needed in Steps 4 and 5; in particular the stated torsion case holds. If $B=0$, $T$ is empty and the empty covering forces every abelian sheaf to have zero sections there, so the same conclusion includes this case.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), proof and (5); homology.tex Tag 010N; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03QO, final proof sentence

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement and split the online Hübner–Schmidt proof into the factor component/residue check, Artin henselian tensor dichotomy, separably closed residue argument, explicit lift-and-glue proof of exact global sections, and the K-injective cohomology calculation. Created two strictly smaller statement-only inputs after DAG, blueprint, Lean and logged Mathlib searches; reused the existing epi, kernel and exact-functor cohomology nodes. No Lean written or compiled.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the Artin joins input in the normal-cone specialization argument of lem-trf-local-term-locality, along its existing Gabber strict-local cohomology-bound ancestry: strict-local intersections are etale acyclic. Steps 1–3 give the tensor-algebra input; Steps 4–5 give its cohomological consequence.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N8-fa914fd9f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, both new nodes, all 12 cited node statements, the parent's Steps 2-3 and unit sk-i-curve-zero. Hübner-Schmidt is not in literature/, so I fetched the PDF and read §6 (p.12), Thm 6.3/6.4 (p.13) and Def 7.8, Prop 7.9, Thm 7.10 with proof (pp.14-15). The item matches the side-DAG base in statement, source, blueprint and unit; only the proof fields, stmt_deps and searches were added, so nothing was weakened. Its statement is the n=2 étale case of Thm 7.10, with the parenthetical given by Prop 7.9. New node lem-trf-artin-henselian-tensor-residue-dichotomy is Thm 6.4 with n=2, hypothesis by hypothesis. Writing n=m∩B_j is forced. Checked on k^sep⊗k^sep, V^sh⊗_V K^sep, and B=0. New node lem-trf-affine-etale-cover-component-criterion is Prop 7.9. The component ring C/I_Z is H-S's colim A/eA. I re-proved both directions for an arbitrary ring: the section on each strictly henselian component spreads to a clopen neighbourhood, compactness of π_0 gives a finite disjoint refinement, and a component with two closed points gives a Zariski cover with no section. I also checked a ring that is not w-local, so the node correctly drops BS's w-local hypothesis. Neither new node duplicates an existing one (grep for quasi-acyclic, w-strictly local, section/split cover; det-pe-* nodes assume w-local) or restates a clause of the item. Steps: (1) uses the criterion and I_Z⊆n; (2) all hypotheses of the dichotomy node are in force; (3) separable algebraic over a separably closed field is trivial, so components are strictly henselian and covers split; (4) the epi lemma plus the section give a disjoint clopen gluing, kernels are sectionwise, so Γ is exact; (5) the K-injective model with the exact-functor Mathlib leaf gives H^q=0, including T empty. proof_deps equals the union of uses and the graph is acyclic. The only off-unit statements cited are Mathlib leaves, so no tool_uses are needed. No SGA is cited. proof_origin is agent with a WANTED line, which is correct since the paper is not local. No fixes.
